| [THEORY-028](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-028.md) v2 | The expected bias of any data-dependent choice, and the expected generalisation error of any learning algorithm, is at most √(2σ²·I) for σ-subgaussian losses, where I is the information the output carries about the data | Russo & Zou (2015), [LIT-356](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-356.md), Prop. 1: \|E[φ_T − µ_T]\| ≤ σ√(2·I(T;φ)) for any selection T among σ-sub-Gaussian statistics. Both proofs rest on Donsker–Varadhan and were checked by the readers. The bound is in expectation only. It is vacuous for deterministic learners on continuous hypotheses, where I(S;W) is infinite, and for any real network when I is bounded by counting bits. It is tight only for Gaussian argmax and threshold selection. | Active |
| [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v2 | Landauer's principle prices only logically irreversible steps, and prices them in exported entropy rather than heat, so acquiring, copying or evaluating a bit, and learning it, carry no minimum thermodynamic cost | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state (erasure, merging of control flow), and it is at least k ln 2 of entropy exported per bit, which "need not" be heat. Goldt & Seifert ([LIT-308](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-308.md)) and Still et al. ([LIT-327](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-327.md)) agree. Information learnt is bounded by entropy production and can be paid almost entirely in weight entropy. The only per-bit heat term is Landauer's, on entropy removed. The synthesis across the three is the record's. It does not license a k_BT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, per gradient step or per bit learnt. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-031.md) | The likelihood-ratio detector is optimal under the payoff, Neyman–Pearson and posterior criteria, which differ only in its threshold, so performance is an ROC and the criterion a point on it; d′ is criterion-free only for equal-variance normal signal and noise | Peterson & Birdsall (1953), [LIT-364](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-364.md) — the threshold on ℓ = f_SN/f_N is optimal for expected value and at fixed false-alarm rate, and the two optimum families coincide (Part I Thms 1–7). The ROC's slope equals the threshold (Thm 8). Tanner & Swets (1954), [LIT-368](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-368.md), carry this over to the human observer as d′ plus a criterion. Stanislaw & Todorov (1999), [LIT-367](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-367.md), state that d′ varies with the criterion unless the variances are equal. The separation of sensitivity from bias is a property of the model, not of the data. | Active |
| [THEORY-035](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-035.md) v5 | Deep networks generalise because the diffusion phase of SGD compresses each layer's information about the input | Shwartz-Ziv & Tishby (2017), [LIT-324](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-324.md), report a fitting phase followed by a long compression phase in the information plane, and read compression by gradient diffusion as the mechanism of generalisation. | [THEORY-039](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-039.md) | The later phases reported in neural-network training differ in kind: after the transition a network may simplify its weights, acquire item-specific information, lose generalisation, confine its tangent kernel or saturate its units, and none of these is a measured compression of I(X;T) | Nanda et al. | [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md) | Training a classifier past zero training error collapses its last-layer features onto their class means and drives the centred means toward a simplex equiangular tight frame, with the classifier aligned to them and the decision becoming nearest class mean | Papyan, Han & Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), measured 480 trained classifiers on seven datasets with VGG, ResNet and DenseNet. Through the terminal phase, within-class variability of last-layer features falls (NC1), and the centred class means become equinorm and equiangular with cosine −1/(C − 1) (NC2). The classifier aligns with them (NC3), and the decision becomes nearest class mean (NC4). They prove that NC1 and NC2 imply NC3 and NC4 for the MSE-optimal and max-margin classifiers, and that the simplex ETF is the unique error-exponent-optimal codebook. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), sees class means separate and grow more orthogonal with depth. The measurements cover one protocol, and the dynamics are unexplained outside free-features models. Within them, THEORY-278 (LIT-974) derives collapse for MSE under a re-whitened flow, and THEORY-286 (LIT-994) gives the cross-entropy endpoint under class imbalance. The paper's further claim, that the Hessian's class outliers are a symptom of collapse, is argued and not measured, and is left to [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) | For experiments on a finite parameter set, being at least as informative for every decision problem is the same as being able to simulate the other by a randomisation | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorem 8 with Theorems 1–3: for experiments with finitely many states and decision problems with bounded losses, α attains every loss vector β attains, in every problem, exactly when a Markov kernel turns α's observation into β's under every state. The direction from simulation to informativeness is Blackwell (1951); the finite converse is Sherman and Stein (1951); the general converse is proved in 1953. It is a qualitative order and says nothing about how much worse an incomparable experiment is. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-161](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-161.md) | In the semantic rate–distortion frameworks of 2021–2025, meaning is a latent variable with a known joint law with the observation, so their limits are indirect source-coding limits; a posterior-matching semantic distortion is, with KL divergence, exactly the information bottleneck, and with total variation a uniform bound on lost decision value | From the readings of Zhao et al. | [THEORY-198](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-198.md) | For a finite-range lattice Hamiltonian, a block coarse-graining that keeps all the mutual information the block shares with the system beyond a buffer makes the coarse measure factorize across the block, so the renormalized Hamiltonian gains no range and, in 1D, product disorder gains no correlations across the block; the coarse-grainings actually optimized fall short of that condition, and for them the link is shown only numerically, in 1D | Lenggenhager, Gökmen, Ringel, Huber and Koch-Janusz (2018), [LIT-881](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-881.md): proved in 1D, and in D dimensions under an extra per-block assumption and barring fine-tuned cancellations. | [THEORY-222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md) | A coarse-grained macro description can carry more effective information than the micro description it supervenes on, so the scale at which a system's causal structure is most effective can be a macro scale | Hoel, Albantakis & Tononi (2013), [LIT-1038](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1038.md), read in [NOTE-726](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-726.md). Effective information is effectiveness (determinism minus degeneracy) times the log of the state-space size, measured under uniform interventions. Coarse-graining always loses size and can gain effectiveness; when the gain wins, causal emergence CE = EI(macro) − EI(micro) is positive. Four toy systems give 0.40 to 2.92 bits. The arithmetic is exact. The reading that the EI peak marks where causation happens rests on imposing a uniform distribution at each level, which the paper adopts and does not test, so the account is Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-227](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-227.md) | Mutual information between an input and its representation does not fix the representation's quality: invertible encoders all preserve it exactly, yet under a linear probe some do better than the raw input and some worse | Tschannen, Djolonga, Rubenstein, Gelly & Lucic (2020), [LIT-247](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-247.md), read in [NOTE-749](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-749.md). Invertible RealNVP encoders on MNIST halves keep the true MI constant, yet trained with an MI estimator they gain linear-probe accuracy, and one trained adversarially against a linear probe ends "significantly worse than using raw pixels". At matched bound values the encoder architecture decides quality. What makes MI-trained representations good must therefore come from somewhere other than MI. The paper's alternative, that InfoNCE works as metric learning, is argued, not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-237](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-237.md) v2 | The critic-based variational lower bounds on mutual information, Donsker–Varadhan, NWJ, MINE's and InfoNCE, are relaxations of one unnormalized Barber–Agakov bound, and each is tight only at a critic equal to the log density ratio up to a term its normalization leaves free | Poole, Ozair, van den Oord, Alemi & Tucker (2019), [LIT-246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-246.md), read in [NOTE-739](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-739.md). Writing q(x\|y) = p(x)e^f/Z(y) in Barber and Agakov's bound gives I_UBA, tight at f = log p(y\|x) + c(y). Jensen gives Donsker–Varadhan, a tangent bound on the log gives TUBA and NWJ (unique optimal critic 1 + log p(x\|y)/p(x)), and NWJ applied to a K-sample problem with the batch mean as normalizer gives InfoNCE. MINE's bias-corrected gradient is the exact gradient of TUBA. A Monte-Carlo DV estimate is neither an upper nor a lower bound. The InfoNCE optimum is cited, not derived, and the bias–variance comparisons are on toys. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-238](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-238.md) v2 | The expected generalization error of an encoder–decoder learner is bounded by the encoder alone, through the KL divergence of its train-and-ghost latents to a prior symmetric under label-preserving permutations, for any decoder, and the bound stays finite for deterministic continuous encoders under lossy compression | Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski (2023), [LIT-245](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-245.md), read in [NOTE-742](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-742.md). Theorem 4: E[gen] ≤ inf 2√((2·MDL + K + 2)/n) + ε, where MDL is the expected KL of the joint law of the latents of the training set and an independent ghost set to any prior invariant under label-preserving permutations, and ε is the distortion allowed by lossy compression. It does not prove that I(X;U) cannot bound generalization. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-240.md) | Loss of consciousness under propofol and in chronic disorders of consciousness goes with reduced pairwise integrated information between default-mode regions that rank as gateways of a synergy-defined workspace, not between its broadcasters | Luppi et al. The gateway/broadcaster split is imposed by the method; only where its two classes fall is measured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-244](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-244.md) | Shannon entropy, mutual information and the distortion-rate function are the expectations of their Kolmogorov counterparts only to within the complexity of the source distribution | Grünwald & Vitányi (2004), [LIT-224](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md), read in [NOTE-776](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-776.md). | [THEORY-257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-257.md) | Dynamical independence, zero information flow from the microscopic history into a coarse-graining given its own history, fixes emergent macroscopic variables by the dynamics rather than by a chosen query, but generically none is exact and the optima are many | Barnett and Seth (2023), [LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), read in [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md): definition (2.6), transitivity (App. A), the causal-graph form (2.12), the state-space closed form (3.18) and the genericity count (3.25)–(3.26). | [THEORY-262](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-262.md) | Neural complexity is low when a system's parts are independent or uniformly dependent and high when small subsets are nearly independent while large ones are integrated; in simulated cortex, patchy grouped connectivity raises it above random connectivity of equal density | Tononi, Sporns & Edelman (1994), [LIT-998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-998.md), read in [NOTE-767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-767.md). C_N, the summed shortfall of average subset integration below a linear rise with subset size, is shown low at both extremes for one family of Gaussian matrices, and higher for patchy than for uniform wiring in one simulated visual area and in small linear systems. All of it is simulation. It is a whole-system number over fixed components: it does not find units or boundaries. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-263](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-263.md) | A coding rate that varies with the realised sample and output makes rate-distortion generalisation bounds data-dependent, and with the rate set to the pointwise information density log dP_{W\|S}/dP(W) against a fixed prior the bound is the disintegrated PAC-Bayes bound | Sefidgaran & Zaidi (2023; IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 2024), [LIT-233](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-233.md), read in [NOTE-806](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-806.md). Theorem 1: with a sample-dependent rate R_{S,W}, gen ≤ √(4σ²(R_{S,W} + log(√(2n)/δ))/(2n−1) + ε). With R_{S,W} = log dP_{W\|S}/dP(W) the coding condition holds at ε = 0 and the bound is the disintegrated PAC-Bayes bound. The general Theorems 3–5 recover Rivasplata et al.'s PAC-Bayes bound and Xu–Raginsky's. The coding construction is proved for finite alphabets only. The general proofs are change of measure. The rate is a Shannon code-length difference against a prior, not Kolmogorov complexity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-266.md) | The average generalisation error along an optimisation trajectory is bounded by the rate-distortion function of the trajectory's law given the sample, plus a coupling term that carries the trajectory's dependence on the sample | Sefidgaran & Zaidi (2023), [LIT-233](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-233.md), Theorem 7, read in [NOTE-806](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-806.md). For an L-Lipschitz loss in [0, 1], with probability ≥ 1 − δ, the mean of gen(S, W^t) over iterations is at most √((RD(S, ε; π_S) + log(√(2n)M/δ))/(2n − 1) + 4Lε). RD is computed for the sample at hand. The coupling coefficient M depends on the unknown distribution and absorbs I(W^T; S). The CIFAR-10 experiment drops M and 4Lε and shows only that the estimated rate and the test gap fall together over learning rates. For FCN4 the plotted rate term is about 3, which is vacuous for 0–1 loss. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-268](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-268.md) | An emergence measure averaged over a system's transitions can be positive while its local value is negative at particular transitions, so emergence so measured belongs to the ensemble, not to each moment | Varley (2022), [LIT-953](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-953.md), read in full in [NOTE-756](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-756.md). Both the coarse-graining and the ΦID accounts of emergence score an expected past–future mutual information, whose pointwise values can be negative. In one constructed toy, about 53% of informative micro transitions map to misinformative macro ones, and the synergy atom is negative for 31.25% of transitions, while both averages are positive. The paper argues the possibility is general and shows it in instances; it does not show that every system flickers, or say what a negative moment means. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-270.md) | Translation without parallel data is learnable from a plausibility prior over the target language alone, with error falling in the common ground between prior and translations, in the size of the source language and in the number of samples | Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise (NeurIPS 2023), [LIT-941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-941.md), read in [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md). Proved for maximum likelihood in stylised random models with uniform languages and one-to-one translators; in one model the bound O(log\|Θ\| / (α·min(m,\|T\|))) is tight up to a constant. Information- theoretic only. The prior substitutes for parallel data in learning the decoder, not for information in a message. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md) | Directional information measures between two symmetrically coupled units follow the path of a recorded drive, not the symmetry of the coupling: flow reads two-way under moderate drive of one unit and one-way under strong drive | Das, Manikandan and Banerjee (2025), [LIT-947](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-947.md), read in [NOTE-788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md). Two colloids are coupled by the fluid through a symmetric tensor, and recorded noise moves one trap. Time-delayed mutual information and transfer entropy give drive → driven → other, with backflow at moderate drive. In numerics only, flow is one-way at strong drive. With no drive the coupled particles are independent at steady state. The paper does not test an unrecorded drive shared by both units, and it does not claim that the measures reveal coupling architecture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-277.md) | For individual data, at every bound on model complexity, the model with the shortest two-part code is, to within O(log n), the best-fitting model in randomness deficiency, although the fit itself cannot be computed or approximated | Vereshchagin & Vitányi (2002/2004), [LIT-239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-239.md), read in [NOTE-787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-787.md), Theorem IV.8: β_x(α) + K(x) and λ_x(α) agree to within O(log n) for a string of length n. Every set minimising K(S) + log \|S\| at complexity α is within O(log n) of the best fit there. h_x and λ_x are upper semicomputable, while β_x is not semicomputable. Restated by Grünwald & Vitányi, [LIT-224](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md), §6.2. Finite-set models; computable distributions at O(log n) cost. It says nothing at the (k/2) log n scale of parametric model selection, and nothing about K(A) + K(x \| A). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-281.md) | Perfect concept erasure caps what a representation can keep at the information not about the concept: if Z is independent of A then I(Z;X) is at most H(X\|A), and a deterministic erasure reaches that cap only when the concept groups' distributions are permutations of one another | Chowdhury et al. (2025), [LIT-963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-963.md), read in full in [NOTE-820](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-820.md). The cap (Lemma 3.3) is a two-line chain-rule argument that needs only the Markov condition A → X → Z. The permutation condition is proved necessary and sufficient for deterministic maps (Appendices A.3 and A.4), with finite supports and disjoint groups. The paper's further statement, that the cap cannot be reached when the groups are not permutations, is false for stochastic maps, which reach it for any finite distributions with disjoint supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-293.md) | For an optimal capacity-bounded learner on a mixture of equally frequent random facts and a second domain, the facts are learned not at all below a capacity threshold set by the mixing ratio and in full above it, and Pythia models trained on such mixtures show the same threshold in model size and in mixing ratio | Gu, Lyu, Li and Zhang (2025), [LIT-984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-984.md), read in [NOTE-796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-796.md). Proved for an idealised learner whose capacity is mutual information with the data (Theorem 4.3), on an orthogonal mixture of uniform facts and a second domain; seen in Pythia models from 14M to 6.9B on synthetic biographies mixed into web text. The theory is static. It does not say when in training the facts arrive, and it does not show that SGD reaches the optimal allocation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-308](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-308.md) | The neural Donsker–Varadhan estimator of mutual information is strongly consistent as an extremum estimator over a compact family of critics, and its uniform deviation from the population bound is controlled by the parameter count, not the data dimension | Belghazi et al. (2018), [LIT-256](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-256.md), §3.3 and App. 8.2.2–8.2.3, read in [NOTE-828](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-828.md). On a compact domain with Lebesgue densities, the supremum of the Donsker–Varadhan bound over some compact network family is within any η of the mutual information, and the empirical supremum converges to the population one almost surely. Uniform deviation ε needs Õ(d log d/ε²) samples for d parameters, under bounded, Lipschitz critics. The guarantee is for the exact empirical maximizer, not for gradient training. The finite-sample estimate is not a bound (Poole et al., [LIT-246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-246.md)), and the proof has two gaps a reading found. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-313](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) | With a kernel normalised to k(x,x) = 1, the covariance operator of a distribution is a density operator, and its quantum relative entropy is a lower bound on the Kullback–Leibler divergence that is tight only for an orthonormal, hence discrete, embedding, lies above the KL of the kernel-smoothed distributions, and on the torus is within O(σ²) of KL as the bandwidth σ shrinks | Bach (2022), [LIT-255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-255.md), read in [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md). Σ_p = ∫ϕϕ* dp is uncentred and unit-trace, so p ↦ Σ_p maps distributions to quantum states, and D(p̃‖q̃) ≤ D(Σ_p‖Σ_q) ≤ D(p‖q) (Proposition 4(d), Eq. 8). The upper bound is joint convexity, with equality only if k(x,y) = 0 for x ≠ y. The lower bound is monotonicity under a measurement whose outcome law is p smoothed by h(x,y) = ⟨ϕ(x), Σ^{−1/2}ϕ(y)⟩². The O(σ²) gap is shown only for translation-invariant kernels on the torus with Lipschitz densities. It does not cover centred kernels, or similarity measures that compare Gram matrices of representations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-352](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-352.md) | A pseudorandom generator exists if and only if a one-way function exists, where both are secure against uniform adversaries and every reduction is an oracle Turing machine, as statements about ensembles indexed by n; the construction from an arbitrary one-way function is only weak-preserving, so security at one length is bought at a much greater one | Håstad, Impagliazzo, Levin and Luby (1999), [LIT-1051](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1051.md), read in [NOTE-880](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-880.md), with Goldreich's Foundations of Cryptography, [LIT-1061](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1061.md), skimmed in [NOTE-863](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-863.md) from the 1995 draft. Theorem 6.2.2: "There are one-way functions iff there are pseudorandom generators." The hard direction runs one-way function → false entropy generator → pseudoentropy generator → generator, by uniform reductions, with seeds of length n^10 in the direct construction. Adversaries are algorithms; the paper has no circuit version, and that the proof carries over to non-uniform adversaries is the reading's inference, not the paper's statement. Everything is asymptotic. Goldreich states the theorem and does not prove it. | Active |
| [THEORY-357](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-357.md) | Computational indistinguishability is strictly coarser than statistical closeness: without any assumption there are ensembles on at most 2^(n/2) strings that no circuit of size 2^(n/8) tells from uniform, though none of them is efficiently samplable, and an efficiently samplable pair of this kind exists if a pseudorandom generator does, since its output covers at most 2^n of the 2^l(n) strings; all of it is about ensembles indexed by n, not single pairs of distributions | Goldreich, Foundations of Cryptography vol. 1, [LIT-1061](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1061.md), read in [NOTE-863](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-863.md) (Skimmed, 1995 draft, Chapters 1–3 in full), with Håstad, Impagliazzo, Levin and Luby (1999), [LIT-1051](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1051.md), read in [NOTE-880](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-880.md). Proposition 3.3 proves by counting that some ensemble far from uniform fools every small circuit; its proof is non-constructive and the ensemble cannot be sampled efficiently. A generator's output is efficiently samplable, indistinguishable from uniform by definition, and statistically far by an image count (§3.3.1). That a samplable such pair exists only if one-way functions do is cited to Goldreich 1990, not read. The book's statistical difference has no factor ½, so it is twice total variation. | Active |
| [THEORY-399](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-399.md) | Storing every inner product of n points of the unit ball of R^k to additive error ε takes Θ(n log n/ε²) bits once k ≥ log n/ε² and Θ(nk log(2 + log n/(ε²k))) below, for 1/n^0.49 ≤ ε ≤ 0.1, and comparing these counts across dimensions shows that some n such points cannot be mapped into fewer than Ω(min{k, log(2 + ε²n)/ε²}) dimensions with additive error ε for every ε ≥ 2/√n; this is a worst-case lower bound with unstated constants, the small-ε bit count is open for k above that dimension, and no one-family embedding that small is proved | Alon and Klartag (2017), [LIT-1151](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1151.md), read in [NOTE-929](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-929.md) from arXiv v4. Theorem 1.1 gives the bits of an additive ε-distance sketch for every k when 1/n^0.49 ≤ ε ≤ 0.1, by a volume argument above and a packing of net points against random probes below. Since an embedding is a sketch, Corollary 2.1 re-proves Larsen and Nelson's bound in that range, and Corollary 2.3, using the Gaussian correlation inequality in place of a union bound, extends it to every ε ≥ 2/√n with log(2 + ε²n) in place of log n. The dimension statements are for additive error on squared distances of points of norm at most 1; the relative form for small ε follows but is not stated. The matching upper bound for one set is open. | Active |
